facts.text: Since I lost my job, I've been focused on building a device to stop people from controlling my mind.

facts.item: how long the withdrawal and low mood have been going on
facts.text: My wife says the withdrawal and the low moods have been going on for the last 3 months.
I was fired from my job 4 weeks ago, after I stopped going to work.
I don't have any significant medical problems.
I've never had any psychiatric problems before.
I've never had a problem with alcohol or other substances.
I don't have any physical health problems.

f001: The source narrates 'bizarre and agitated behavior' without saying who reports it; it is worded as what his wife says, since she gives collateral history and the patient would not call his own behavior bizarre.
f007: The source gives low mood both as the wife's report (history) and as a secondary symptom; worded as the patient's own experience, with the 3-month span attributed to the wife (f008).

source_issues: Secondary symptoms include observer-only signs ('Disorganized speech', 'Psychomotor agitation') and a diagnostic label ('Delusions of persecution').

excluded_sources.reason: 'Disorganized speech' is an observer-only sign; already in the mental status examination (x005, speech: rapid, disorganized).
'Psychomotor agitation' is an observer-only sign; already in the mental status examination (x005, appearance: agitated).

notes: Psychiatric content is written as what the patient believes (the NSA spies on him and controls his mind; he is building a device against it), not as the label 'delusions of persecution' (p002 cited for f003 and f004).
Collateral history from the wife (withdrawal, intermittent low mood over 3 months) is worded as what he was told.
The 3-month span covers both the withdrawal and the low mood, so it is a standalone fact (f008).
Appearance, behavior and speech are grouped as one mental status examination record (x005); the neurological components stay separate. The toxicology screen is one ordered panel (x014).

'No significant medical or psychiatric history' gives two denials (f011, f012). 'No history of substance abuse' (f014) and 'denies any drug use' (f013) are kept as two statements: abuse covers alcohol, use covers current drugs.
'No significant findings' in the review of systems carries no meaning beyond the listed denials.

extras.objective_for_doctor: Assess and manage a young man brought in by his wife for bizarre and agitated behavior, suspecting a possible psychiatric disorder.
